outcomes: A user who declares one extension gets every extension its manifest depends on, transitively, without declaring them
The lock pins every extension of the graph, so a fresh worktree and a hosted run restore the same graph
Under an explicit channel, the whole graph resolves on that channel, so init on a channel never reads latest
nonGoals: Writing a dependency into putnami.workspace.json: the workspace keeps the roots its user wrote
A new lock field or lock format version: the lock binds each manifest by hash, and the manifests carry the edges
Opting into a dependency's agent content because it installed
Dependencies in the user scope, which has no workspace file to name its roots
Counting dependencies as workspace-wide consumers in impact analysis

requirements.text: putnami install, putnami extensions install and putnami init install from the registry every registry-named extension that an extension loaded from the artifact store or from a declared workspace path lists in extensionDependencies, transitively, and pin each one in putnami.lock.json as an ordinary extension entry. putnami.workspace.json is never written for a dependency.

Only putnami.workspace.json satisfies a dependency, by name or by a path whose manifest has that name. A global-configuration key that names a graph member is ignored with one warning. An undeclared workspace project of a dependency's name is set aside, whether or not the lock pins the dependency, and never loads in its place.

An explicit channel, in the portable channel alphabet and other than latest, from --channel, PUTNAMI_CHANNEL or the install record during init, or from a name@channel argument, flows down: every dependency below the requested extension resolves on it at every hop, and its own constraint is checked against the resolved version. A semantic version or a range is not a channel. Otherwise a non-empty constraint resolves as written, the registry picking the highest match, and an empty one on latest.

A locked dependency resolves from its lock entry while it satisfies every constraint known when it resolves. An explicit channel named on the command line re-resolves the requested subgraph, --latest and putnami upgrade re-resolve the graph, and a locked version that misses a constraint resolves again and the move is reported.

A resolved version that misses a semantic-version range, or a channel answer without a resolved version when a range must be checked, fails the install. The error names the dependency, its version and each dependent with its constraint, also for a dependency the workspace declares by name.

The graph resolves level by level, whatever order the workers finish in: dependents resolved under an explicit channel first, then dependents by manifest name, then dependencies by name. A node resolves once, at its first level, and a dependency reached earlier from outside a channel's subgraph keeps its request, and the channel only checks it. A later-level constraint is only checked, and a cycle installs each extension once.

Discovery loads every locked dependency of a loaded extension from the artifact store, after the declared extensions. An extension that only the root package.json development dependencies declare does not load, installed in node_modules or not. Context generation, option ownership and the missing-extension check include dependencies. A dependency that does not load is reported with the extension that requires it, and removing its only dependent stops loading it.

The bootstrap restore and the MCP read preparation restore each locked dependency of a restored extension, and never resolve one the lock does not pin: they report it with its dependent and putnami install.
An agent-content opt-in may name any extension of the graph.

A dependency the workspace does not declare loses every reserved provider command: credential provider, cache provider, runner provider, session reporter, log reporter and Cloud release set. Discovery records each removal and putnami extensions list names it.

putnami extensions update and putnami upgrade re-resolve every dependency by the resolution rules, write its lock entry and never write it into the workspace file's pins. update --dry-run previews the declared extensions only, and says so. putnami extensions list shows each dependency with the extension that requires it.

When putnami extensions update, putnami templates update, putnami upgrade, install --latest or install name@channel resolves a locked artifact again on a channel (latest, an empty constraint, * or a channel name), it never moves the pin to an older build or to one whose version does not compare with it: it keeps the pin, leaves its lock entry as it is and names the channel and the build it serves. Only an exact version or a range moves a pin backwards, and ↑ marks only a newer version.

putnami extensions remove refuses when the name is still reachable from the workspace declarations without it, and names the members on that path, so the root of a cycle can be removed. Otherwise it removes the lock entry of the name and of each dependency those declarations no longer reach.
A hosted run installs the graph from the committed lock and writes no lock. A dependency the lock does not pin fails the install, as an unpinned declared extension does.
putnami extensions install --user refuses an extension whose manifest names a registry dependency, and names the limit.

A CLI that predates the dependency rung refuses a manifest that names a registry dependency as requiring a newer putnami. This CLI skips such a manifest stamped below the rung, whether it loads from the artifact store or from a declared path, with the reason, and follows none of its dependencies.
